subject: Operations
title: The COVID Supply Chain Crisis
description: One-minute skill: The COVID Supply Chain Crisis.

hook.text: In 2020, toilet paper vanished. Chips ran out. Shipping containers cost 10 times normal. The global supply chain broke.

buildup.text: COVID-19 hit supply and demand simultaneously—factories closed while consumer buying patterns shifted overnight.

discovery.text: Port congestion, container shortages, and labor gaps created a cascading bottleneck that took two years to clear.

twist.text: The crisis wasn't just about the virus—decades of lean optimization had removed every buffer in the system.

climax.text: Companies that diversified suppliers and held strategic buffers recovered months faster than ultra-lean rivals.

punchline.text: Lean was efficient—until the world stopped.

quiz.question: Why did lean supply chains struggle during COVID?
